metrics.method: Manual read of all 457 non-service messages in data/chats/barbara-x-altr.jsonl (2026-07-20T17:26 -> 2026-09-24T09:17): 249 from the client (Barb Brazil, per client_aliases in config/clients.yaml) and 208 from our side (Mayson 38, Stephski 35, Olivia 32, Derrek 32, Michelle 27, Vivek 24, Mica 20 — all direct ALTR staff per config/team.yaml; no vendor chat team operates in this group). Counts extend the 2026-09-18 pass forward over the Sep 18-24 window using the same rules. 'Client question' = a client message containing an explicit ask, punctuated or not; a multi-message ask counts once. A naive '?' count over the raw file gives 43; the manual figure is higher because many asks are unpunctuated. 'Unanswered >24h' = never answered, answered only after 24h, or acknowledged with no substance (a tag, an emoji, 'We will check'). ~10 new asks landed Sep 18-24 and ~7 are unanswered, including the terminal device-safety question asked three times. 'Promise' = an explicit first-person commitment by our side to do or send something; 'kept' = evidenced in chat; 'lapsed' = never delivered and never mentioned again. 3 commitments made Sep 21-22 are still technically in-window and counted as neither. Derrek's Sep 19 'we got both of your backup accounts back' is counted as kept-then-reversed (1 kept), since the client contradicted it within 24h. max_team_silence_days computed from consecutive our-side timestamps: 3.82d (Sep 10 18:04 -> Sep 14 13:43), then 3.77d (Sep 4 -> Sep 8), 3.19d (Aug 27 -> Aug 30), and notably 2.17d (Sep 17 15:46 -> Sep 19 19:51) which falls entirely inside the ban crisis.

Stephski's billing honesty. She caught her own $1,683.12 under-billing, disclosed it with the full arithmetic shown rather than burying it, and told the client to take her time. Five invoices, five paid, zero disputes — she is the only person on this account with a perfect close rate.
top_fix: Give this account one named owner who closes loops in writing, and make a weekly written status containing at least one real number a non-negotiable deliverable. Every failure here is the same failure wearing a different hat: we reply in 43 minutes and we close in never — 23 lapsed promises, 29 unanswered asks, a client-written rescue plan sitting 32 days without a yes or no, and a retention warning that got a call offer and no call. A single owner posting 'here is what we posted, here is what it did, here is every open item with a date and a name' every Friday would have surfaced the traffic collapse in week two instead of letting her find it in her own OnlyFans dashboard in week eight; would have made it impossible for a Meta-support rep to re-promise the same account recovery four times in eight weeks; and would have caught the one thing that actually ends this relationship — a frightened client asking the same question three times, getting silence, and going quiet for the first time in 67 days while the only messages in her chat were about her rather than to her.
